To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HDL and Sphingosine‐ 1‐phosphate promote Stat3 activation, cell migration and invasion in prostate cancer DU 145 cells via ERKI/2 and S 1P receptors.

HDL and Sphingosine‐ 1‐Phosphate activate Stat3 in prostate cancer cells through the activation of S1P receptor 1, 3, and 5, and that this activation promotes prostate cancer cell migration and invasion.
HDL and Sphingosine‐ 1‐Phosphate activate Stat3 in DU145 cells via the ERK1/ 2 and S1PR1/3 pathways and promote DU145 cell migration and invasion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of HDl on prostate cancer cells.
the role of HDL in prostate cancer progression.
the effect of HDLDL and sphingosin-1-phosphate (S1p) on Stat3 activation and cell proliferation in three prostate cancer cells (PC-3, LNCap and DU145) and the role of S1p receptor in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HDL activates Stat3 via S1P in prostate cancer cells, and this process is dependent on S1P receptor 2 and ERK1/ 2 activation.
HDL and Sph1P activate Stat3 via S1P receptors and the ERK1/ERK2 pathway in DU145 prostate cancer cells, and promote their migration and invasion.
HDL and S‐1‐P activate STAT3 in prostate cancer cells via the ERK1/ 2 pathway and S1P receptor 1 and 2, and promote cell motility and invasion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HDL and Sphingosine‐ 1‐phosphate promote prostate cancer cell migration and invasion through the activation of Stat3, which is mediated by the S1P receptor and the ERK1/ 2 pathway.
HDL and Sphingosine‐phosphate (SP) activate Stat3 via ERK1‐2 and S1‐P receptors, and this process promotes cell migration and invasion.
HDL, S1P and sphingosylphosphorylcholine (SPC) activate Stat3 in prostate cancer cells via ERK and S1P receptor 1, and promote cell motility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HDL and SphK1/S1P signaling are important in the progression of prostate cancer, and may be a potential target for prostate cancer therapy.
Stat3 activation by HDL and Sphingosine‐ 1‐phosphate in prostate cancer cells is mediated via S1P receptors and ERK1/ 2.
HDL and Sphingosine‐ 1‐phosphate promote cell migration and invasive behavior of DU145 cells via activation of Stat3.
